relationships.subject: hydrogen-rich water
relationships.evidence_quote: This study showed that the systemic therapeutic treatment with HRW inhibited the mechanical allodynia, thermal hyperalgesia and thermal allodynia induced by CCI and the emotional deficits associated in mice.

relationships.subject: SnPP
relationships.evidence_quote: The results showed that the mechanical antiallodynic (Figure 4A) and thermal antihyperalgesic (Figure 4B) actions produced by HRW were reversed with its co-administration with SnPP, dicoumarol and glibenclamide

relationships.subject: CoPP
relationships.evidence_quote: Data showed that the co-administration of CoPP with HRW produced a greater analgesic effect than that made by both treatments administered separately

relationships.subject: hydrogen-rich water
relationships.evidence_quote: In the DRG, there was also a reduction on the HO-1 expression in CCI-mice treated with VEH (p < 0.05, one-way ANOVA vs. sham-operated mice treated with VEH), which was reversed by HRW treatment (Figure 7A).

relationships.subject: hydrogen-rich water
relationships.evidence_quote: In the DRG, nerve injury increased the expression of p-IKBα (Figure 9A), p-AKT (Figure 9B), BAX (Figure 9C) and 4-HNE (Figure 9D) (p < 0.05, one-way ANOVA vs. sham-operated mice treated with VEH) and all of them were inhibited with HRW treatment.

key_findings: Hydrogen-rich water reverses CCI-induced allodynia/hyperalgesia and anxiety/depressive-like behaviors in mice, dependent on HO-1, NQO1 and KATP channels.
CoPP (HO-1 inducer) synergizes with HRW; HRW normalizes HO-1 downregulation in DRG and amygdala.
